Definition
[Geometrically tame end] 1. Definition 8.11.2\group geometric tamenessSource: thurston:page-0233, thurston:page-0234 Let $P$ be cusp horoball neighborhoods and $M$ the convex hull. An end $E$ of $N-P$ with incompressible boundary surface $S\subset M$ is geometrically tame if either $E\cap M$ is compact or the family of uncrumpled surfaces homotopic to $S$ and eventually contained in $E$ is noncompact. A manifold is geometrically tame when it has a compact core whose complementary ends are geometrically tame.
